metadata.name: M20J
metadata.copyrightInfo: Expanded introduction based on N5772R POH Manual 1227

items.prompt: Rev Switch on top right of panel does failover of the GI-275.

GEAR SAFETY OVERRIDE SWITCH. This electrically bypasses the airspeed safety switch. In the event the gear control switch is inadvertently placed in the gear-up position, the gear airspeed safety switch prevents the gear being retracted before approximately 65 KTS airspeed is reached. Should it be necessary-to retract at lower airspeed the gear safety override switch may be pressed allowing the gear to retract.
Beware that this can cause gear to start retracting on the ground!
Failure to pull the Landing Gear switch out before up or down can break the switch.
New to complex aircraft: the Annunciator/Gear Lights test and the panel of caution lights above are critical information. Get in the habit of reading this panel every time, not just glancing at it.
There is no circuit breaker for the Electric trim - note position of the switch instead.

The landing gear is electrically actuated (motor under the rear seat driving a mechanical linkage). Debris/bird nests, a bent door or damaged linkage here can prevent gear extension and retraction — this is a safety-critical inspection point.
Club policy is to refuel tanks to 25 gal/side.
A pitot system drain valve is located on the forward bottom skin of the left wing just outboard of the wing root. The static system also has a drain just rearward of the left wing.
The M20J wing is a laminar-flow airfoil, and noticeably more sensitive to leading-edge contamination — bugs, frost, even paint chips can measurably raise stall speed and degrade handling.
This aircraft has NO elevator trim tab. Pitch trim is achieved by moving the entire horizontal stabilizer, controlled by the console trim wheel.
Engine Oil Level (Min 5 qts, Max 7 qts)

The constant-speed prop's pitch-change mechanism is oil-actuated through the hub. Check the spinner and hub area for oil staining/leaks, not just nicks on the blades; a leak here is a governor-system problem, not just cosmetic.
Only the left pilot seat has brakes!!

items.prompt: Because there's no trim tab, the wheel is geared low, so it takes more turns and more deliberate motion than trim wheels on the club's other aircraft — don't let a student assume a quick flick is enough.

items.expectation: CHECK EGT ALL CYL(MAX 175 RPM, DIFF 50 RPM)

items.prompt: There is no alternator field switch, check alternator through load only, DO NOT turn of master else.

items.expectation: PRESS AND HOLD TEST - 5 BEEPS, VERIFY ALL ANNUNCIATORS FLASH & TURN OFF
FORWARD & AFT - VERIFY NO TRIM MOVEMENT
FORWARD & AFT - VERIFY NO TRIM MOVEMENT
VERIFY TRIM WHEEL RUNS NOSE DOWN
VERIFY TRIM WHEEL RUNS NOSE UP
HOLD DISC & ACTUATE MET - VERIFY NO MOVEMENT
ROTATE LEFT & RIGHT - VERIFY YOKE FOLLOWS BUG
PRESS & HOLD - VERIFY SERVOS RELEASE, RELEASE TO RE-ENGAGE
HOLD PITCH UP/DOWN - VERIFY TRIM WHEEL RUNS AFTER 3 SEC
PRESS - VERIFY AP DISENGAGES & TONE SOUNDS

items.prompt: The red Emergency Gear Extension T-handle check is critical.
Landing Gear (Positive Rate) no runway remaining
Positive rate first, THEN gear up — resist retracting early.
100 KIAS is preferred to 88 KIAS Vy
This airplane is sluggish in the climb if the nose comes up before reaching Vy. Hold the correct attitude and let the airspeed build to the target before demanding more climb.

items.expectation: FULL RICH (LEAN ABOVE 5000 MSL FOR MAX POWER)

items.prompt: See the visor for cruise performance combinations at various altitudes.

items.expectation: LEAN TO PEAK EGT OR 50-100°F ROP

items.prompt: The JPI EDM-830 engine monitor gives per-cylinder EGT/CHT. Teach students to lean off the *first* cylinder to peak, not an average — leaning to an average EGT can leave the actual leanest cylinder dangerously lean of peak.
Begin slowing down and descending EARLY. The M20J is clean and slippery, and slips are largely ineffective.
Retarding throttle below 12" MP causes gear warning horn if gear retracted.
Avoid continuous operation between 1500-1950 RPM below 15" MP
Select a new tank before nearing the destination, no need to add a fuel problem close to landing.
Tie gear extension into the broader early-deceleration habit from the Before Approach/Descent note rather than treating it as a last-second box to check.

items.expectation: CHECK GEAR SAFE LIGHT & VISUAL FLOOR INDICATOR

items.prompt: The floor-mounted visual gear indicator (mechanical alignment marks, independent of the electrical gear-down lights) is a Mooney-specific backup. Teach students to actually check it, not just glance past it — it's there specifically because it can't fail the same way an electrical indication can.

items.expectation: CHECK GEAR SAFE & VISUAL FLOOR INDICATOR

checklists.title: Failure of Landing Gear to Extend Electrically

items.prompt: An electric gear failure is a real, not-uncommon Mooney event, and the manual extension sequence (12-20 pulls) is physical and can be fumbled under stress. Mentally prepare.
Slowly pull T-Handle 1-2 inches to rotate clutch mechanism and allow it to engage drive shaft

items.expectation: 12-20 INCHES & RETURN UNTIL GEAR DOWN LIGHT ILLUMINATED (12-20 PULLS)

checklists.title: Failure to Retract Landing Gear Electrically

items.prompt: GEAR UNSAFE and GEAR DOWN lights
Check AIRSPEED safety switch as soon as practicable
If above procedures do not initiate retraction process, check emergency manual extension lever on floor for proper position.
Gear DOWN for paved runway or smooth surface; Gear UP for rough fields, soft ground, or trees
Gear DOWN for paved runway or smooth surface; Gear UP for rough fields, soft ground, or trees
